title: Commit to the Work
excerpt: Faithful with what God gives, trusting Him with what we can't control. Our job is obedience; God's job is everything else.

blocks.text: It's a complex dance—being faithful with the opportunities God gives you while also trusting Him with the variables that are out of your control.
The writer of Proverbs, typically attributed to King Solomon, said this:

verses: Commit your work to the Lord, and your plans will be established.

blocks.text: It sounds simple enough—to commit your work to the Lord. But it takes intentional effort, continual surrender, and genuine trust.
Throughout Scripture, we see all kinds of work: farming, building, pastoring, parenting, fishing, doctoring, leading, designing, singing, writing, engineering, shepherding, and much more.
In his letter to the Roman believers, Paul discusses talents and gifts when he says:

verses: In his grace, God has given us different gifts for doing certain things well. So if God has given you the ability to prophesy, speak out with as much faith as God has given you. If your gift is serving others, serve them well. If you are a teacher, teach well. If your gift is to encourage others, be encouraging. If it is giving, give generously. If God has given you leadership ability, take the responsibility seriously. And if you have a gift for showing kindness to others, do it gladly.

blocks.text: You can commit your work to God by:

items: valuing the people you interact with
leveraging your God-given creativity to glorify Him

blocks.text: You can plant a seed in good soil, position it for ideal sunlight, and water it consistently, but—above all—it's God who gave you the seed and it's God who makes the seed grow.
Our job is obedience, God's job is everything else. So whatever you do, commit your work, your efforts, and your life to Him—and watch Him work through you.
